items.question: What is semantic search?
items.answer: Semantic search retrieves results based on meaning rather than exact keyword matches. Text is converted into embeddings — numeric representations of meaning — so a query can match relevant content even when it uses different words.

items.question: How much does semantic search development cost?
items.answer: A semantic search platform typically costs $25,000–$70,000 and takes 8–16 weeks. Hybrid search combining vector and keyword retrieval for RAG runs $35,000–$80,000 over 10–16 weeks.

items.question: Does semantic search replace keyword search?
items.answer: Usually not. Hybrid search combines both: semantic retrieval for meaning and keyword retrieval for exact terms such as part numbers, names and codes.

items.question: Can semantic search work with our existing search engine?
items.answer: Often yes. Many teams add vector search alongside an existing keyword index rather than replacing it. We assess your current stack during discovery.

items.question: Who owns the search system?
items.answer: You do — code, ingestion pipelines, indices, evaluation datasets and documentation are transferred at completion.
